Technical SEO.title: Google Helpful Content Doc With New Main Content & EOT/SA Sections
Technical SEO.summary: Google updated its helpful, reliable, people-first content guidance to add two new sections covering the critical role of main content and how Search Quality raters evaluate main content quality. The update also adds new EOT and SA sections to the documentation.

Technical SEO.title: Google Adds Fake Author Warning To Helpful Content Guidance
Technical SEO.summary: Google has updated its people-first content guidance to explicitly warn site owners against fabricated author profiles, formalizing a signal that its Search Quality Rater Guidelines already addressed. Enterprise content teams publishing at scale should audit author E-E-A-T signals accordingly.

Technical SEO.title: Google Tests URL Tracking Parameters To AI Overviews & AI Mode
Technical SEO.summary: Google is testing the addition of tracking parameters to link URLs within AI Overviews, which would allow site owners to distinguish clicks originating from AI Overviews versus standard web results in analytics. If rolled out fully, this would give enterprise SEOs a direct attribution signal for AI Overview traffic.

Technical SEO.title: Search News Buzz Video Recap: Google Spam Update Impact, Google Not Paying Much For Your Content, Google Feels Sad & Terrible and more
Technical SEO.summary: The recap covers the first and second waves of impact from the Google September 2026 spam update, along with discussion of the AI contribution report. Enterprise sites should monitor rankings closely given the multi-wave rollout pattern.

Technical SEO.title: October 2026 Google Webmaster Report: Spam Update, Gemini 3.8, AI Contribution & Monopoly Rulings
Technical SEO.summary: A monthly webmaster report summarizing the Google September 2026 spam update, Gemini 3.8 developments, AI contribution features, and ongoing monopoly ruling implications. Useful as a consolidated reference for enterprise SEO teams tracking algorithm and policy changes.

Digital Marketing / Martech.title: When A Search Query Becomes A Standing Instruction
Digital Marketing / Martech.summary: Google AI Mode and OpenAI are shifting search toward persistent, ongoing monitoring tasks rather than one-off queries, raising new questions about site visibility when requests remain active over time. This has direct implications for how brands think about maintaining presence in AI-driven search surfaces.

Digital Marketing / Martech.title: Shopify Now Enrolls Your Store In Every New AI Shopping Channel
Digital Marketing / Martech.summary: Shopify is now automatically opting merchants into new AI shopping channels, including Meta and unnamed startups, via the agentic storefronts setting. Brands with Shopify storefronts should audit this setting to control where their product data surfaces across AI commerce channels.

AI Search / GEO.title: AI Overviews Currently Appear for 83% of Branded Searches
AI Search / GEO.summary: Ahrefs research finds that AI Overviews now appear for 83% of branded queries, potentially reducing direct clicks to brand websites and amplifying third-party sources such as Wikipedia and YouTube. This is a critical visibility risk for enterprise brands in travel, automotive, and other verticals managing branded search equity.

AI Search / GEO.title: How We Build An SEO Content Roadmap For The AI Search Era (Step-By-Step)
AI Search / GEO.summary: Search Engine Journal outlines a step-by-step process for constructing an SEO content roadmap that accounts for AI Overviews, moving from keyword gap analysis to a prioritized, citation-ready content plan. The structured approach is relevant for enterprise teams aligning content strategy with AI answer-surface visibility.

AI Search / GEO.title: Judge Dismisses Chegg and Penske Antitrust Lawsuits Targeting Google AI Search
AI Search / GEO.summary: A federal judge has dismissed antitrust lawsuits brought by Chegg and Penske against Google AI search, signaling that legal challenges to AI Overviews reducing publisher traffic face a high bar. Enterprise SEO and content teams should interpret this as confirmation that adapting to AI search surfaces, rather than relying on regulatory relief, is the path forward.
